conventions.convention: Signature is (-,+,+,+); manifold orientation is independent of time orientation. The Hodge star satisfies α ∧ *β = ⟨α,β⟩g vol_g.
Observer covectors are E_a=cF_ab n^b and B_a=-(*F)_ab n^b. In a positively oriented observer tetrad, F_0i=-E_i/c, F_ij=ε_ijk B_k, and ε_123=+1.
Coordinates have length units, x^0=ct, ρ=j^0/c, J^i=j^i, and ε₀=(μ₀c²)⁻¹. No exact numerical value for μ₀ is adopted.

Point-normal component derivatives act on the defined chart-component functions, rather than components of a varying observer congruence. Global component equations require a fixed Minkowski inertial chart and constant observer.
Charge is Q(Σ)=c⁻¹∫Σ i_j vol_g. Integration uses finite smooth singular chains with alternating signed face boundary; spacelike chains use the future-normal orientation.
All three items explicitly assume Countable Choice. Their conclusions are conditional deductions or pointwise computations, with no reported measurements or empirical confirmation.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated smooth oriented Lorentzian geometry, d(*F)=-i_v vol_g with v^b=∇_aF^{ab}; hence ∇_aF^{ab}=-μ₀j^b iff d(*F)=μ₀i_j vol_g. The sourced equation implies ∇_aj^a=0. Its local component identities hold pointwise in positively oriented normal coordinates.

Under the stated smooth Maxwell equations, every finite smooth singular three-chain Σ satisfies Q(Σ)=(μ₀c)⁻¹∫∂Σ *F. Every finite smooth three-chain V satisfies ∫∂V F=0. If ∂C=Σ₂-Σ₁+B for a finite smooth four-chain C, then Q(Σ₂)-Q(Σ₁)=-Q(B).

Under its stated geometric and fixed-sector variational hypotheses, T^{00}=(ε₀|E|²+μ₀⁻¹|B|²)/2, T^{0i}=(E×B)_i/(μ₀c), and T^{ij}=-ε₀(E_iE_j-δ_ij|E|²/2)-μ₀⁻¹(B_iB_j-δ_ij|B|²/2) in a positively oriented orthonormal observer tetrad; the tensor is symmetric and trace-free.
The displayed Cartesian two-form F_b on ℝ×(ℝ³\{0}) is smooth and closed, has outward unit-sphere flux 4πb, and has no global one-form potential when b≠0.
